card.statement:
Suppose that
$V$ is $\Z_+$-graded, so that $V=\bigoplus_{i\geq 0}V_i$,
and that $V_0=\C\vac$.
Then $\gr V$ and $R_V$ are equipped with the induced grading:

\begin{align*}
&\gr V= \bigoplus_{i\geq 0}(\gr V)_i,\quad (\gr V)_0=\C,\\
&R_V=\bigoplus_{i\geq 0}(R_V)_i,\quad (R_V)_0=\C.
\end{align*}

So
the following conditions are equivalent:

- $V$ is lisse.

- $X_V=\{0\}$.

- The image of any vector $a\in V_i$ for $i\geq 1$ in $\gr V$ is
nilpotent.

- The image of any vector $a\in V_i$ for $i\geq 1$ in $R_V$ is nilpotent.

Thus,
lisse vertex algebras can be regarded as a generalization of
finite-dimensional algebras.
card.label: Remark 46
